thread:
Alex: @channel GPUs in us-west2 are saturated, cluster-autoscaler is thrashing, and tons of pods are Pending in namespace `ml`. Need immediate containment. (08:12 UTC)

SRE-Bot: [ALERT] cluster-autoscaler: multiple scale-up/scale-down cycles detected for nodepool=gpu-usw2. Recent events: scaleUp count=9 in 6m, scaleDown count=7 in 6m.

Maria: Running quick checks — `kubectl get pods -n ml --field-selector=status.phase==Pending -o wide | wc -l` -> ~320 pending.

Kai: Copy. Are these new job launches or a runaway deployment? Any high-replica job triggered?

Priya: I see a Deployment `runner-heavy` with `replicas: 600` in the ml namespace (accidentally set by a CI job). It created many pods requesting 1 GPU each.

Alex: Ok that's the culprit. Priority: stop new pods from launching, then drain/evict safely where possible.

Jonah: On it — I'm going to scale that deployment to 0 now: `kubectl scale deployment runner-heavy -n ml --replicas=0`

Priya: Thanks. Also patch the HPA / job controller to prevent immediate relaunches: `kubectl annotate deployment runner-heavy prevent-restart=true -n ml` (we'll remove annotation after).

Maria: While we stop the source, the CA is still creating nodes. Suggest we temporarily pause cluster-autoscaler to prevent further thrasher spin-ups.

Kai: Agreed. On GKE we can scale the CA Deployment to 0 replicas. `kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment cluster-autoscaler --replicas=0` — will do that now.

SRE-Bot: [INFO] cluster-autoscaler scaled down to 0 replicas by user Kai.

OpsOnCall: Tainting new GPU nodes so non-critical pods don't land on them: `kubectl taint nodes -l nodepool=gpu-usw2 emergency=isolated:NoSchedule` — applying. This prevents further evictions/placement churn.

Alex: Good. After taint, we should cordon the yet-unused nodes that CA already created and consider deleting excess nodes to avoid cost. But first make sure critical workloads are not affected.

Priya: Verified `runner-heavy` replicas are 0 and most Pending pods are controllers for that deployment; deleting them frees scheduler backlog. `kubectl delete pods -l app=runner-heavy -n ml --force --grace-period=0` ran. Pending count dropped from ~320 -> ~18 (other unrelated jobs).

Maria: Now uncordon the nodes that host production critical pods and keep taint on the rest. `kubectl uncordon gpu-prod-01 gpu-prod-02` — production remains healthy.

Kai: Deleting extra nodepool nodes: I filed a drain job for nodes with taint emergency=isolated, then deleted ones in cloud console. We reclaimed ~24 nodes.

SRE-Bot: [INFO] Cloud API: terminated 24 instances in managed instance group gpu-usw2-pool.

Jonah: Cost note — if CA had kept scaling for another hour we'd have added ~$6k in spot/ondemand GPU costs. We should add safeguards in infra to avoid runaway replica counts.

OpsOnCall: Filed a quota/ASG safety rule: reject creation of >50 GPU pods per namespace per 5m window via admission webhook. Will draft PR.

Priya: Short-term mitigation checklist we applied: 1) scale culprit deployment to 0 2) pause CA 3) taint new nodes 4) delete pending pods 5) delete excess nodes 6) uncordon prod nodes. All done.

Alex: Can someone open an incident ticket and add timeline + commands we ran? Also add follow-ups: admission webhook, CI guardrails (cap replicas), alert to owners when >50 GPU pods spawn in 10m, and make cluster-autoscaler less aggressive for GPU pools.

Kai: Creating the incident doc now. I'll assign follow-ups to infra and devex.

Jonah: For longer-term, consider an autoscaler profile for GPU pools with: higher scaleUpDelay, conservative max surge, and a per-namespace quota cap. Also add preemptible/spot fallback pool to absorb spikes cheaper.

Maria: Noted. I'm adding a runbook step to prefer taint-and-evict vs immediate node deletion for safety.

SRE-Bot: [RESOLVED] Alert cleared — GPU allocatable stabilized to 85% after cleanup.

Alex: Thanks everyone. Postmortem to follow. Action items: admission webhook PR, CI guard, CA profile change, cost alert for rapid GPU spend. :thumbsup:
